title: Ghost-scroll smoothing and adaptive column-gesture presets for dense data grids
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In dense, virtualized tables we observe an intermittent UX issue users call 'ghost scroll' where rapid scrolling reveals header/column misalignment, temporary blank rows, or incorrect hover affordances. Additionally, column-resize gestures feel unstable at high density and on touch devices: users accidentally toggle sort, overshoot sizes, or lose context while resizing. Goal: design a cohesive set of fixes and affordances that 1) eliminate ghost scroll visual artifacts without regressing throughput, 2) provide adaptive column-gesture presets (fast/precise modes) that respect density modes, and 3) improve discoverability for sorting/filtering interactions in compact views.
background: We have many prior tickets addressing parts of this problem, but they are fragmented (virtualization tuning, header reflow, and density presets are separate). This ticket consolidates the design work and produces a high-fidelity pattern that engineering can implement along with clear acceptance criteria and a lightweight experiment plan.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce 'scroll sentinels' at virtualization boundaries to stabilize measured scroll height and avoid transient blank regions. 2) Add velocity-aware resizing: short fast drags snap to coarse presets; long slow drags enable fine-grain pixels. 3) Expose a density-aware resize affordance: in compact density, present a grab-target with +/- presets; in regular/dense the snap presets default to narrower steps. 4) Show a transient size preview overlay with keyboard accessibility and ARIA announcements on resize/snap. 5) Add a subtle persistent hint in header toolbar to toggle precise resize mode and a contextual cue when sort/filter controls are hidden due to density.
tradeoffs: Performance: sentinels add small extra DOM measurement and bookkeeping—cost vs perceived stability must be benchmarked.
Complexity: velocity-based gestures increase gesture handler complexity; need cross-platform testing (mouse, trackpad, touch, stylus).
Discoverability vs clutter: adding persistent hints may increase header density; prefer transient microcopy and first-time coachmarks.
Persistence: per-user column width persistence improves UX but increases storage surface area and migration considerations for schema changes.
out_of_scope: Full RTL overhaul (will be tested but not redesigned here)
Server-side virtualization algorithm changes (handled in ENG tickets)
Embedding column reordering heuristics beyond basic resize + snap
acceptance_criteria: No reproducible ghost-scroll visual gap in acceptance tests (automated scroll replay for common data heights).
Column resize supports two interaction modalities: coarse snap (fast drag) and fine-grain (slow drag / keyboard) in all densities.
Transient size preview overlay appears and is screen-reader announced; keyboard-only users can resize by focus + arrow keys and get same presets.
Density toolbar hides non-critical sort/filter affordances only when space-constrained, and shows a discoverable overflow control to access them.
Performance: end-to-end median scroll frame time does not regress more than 5% in our perf harness compared to baseline.
Design sign-off from PM and Eng leads and a small closed beta with 3 internal teams showing improved perceived stability.

notes_for_engineering: Sentinel implementation should be togglable via table prop (enableGhostSmoothing) with default on for console tables.
Expose resizePresets: array of pixel widths and a mode enum {auto, coarse-first, precise-first}.
Instrumentation hooks: emit events on resize start/end, snap applied (preset id), and ghost-smoothing toggles for analytics.
Provide a simple CSS-only fallback for older browsers where JS gesture detection is unavailable.
Add e2e test IDs to header elements to enable automated scroll replay verification.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Sentinels could introduce layout thrashing. Mitigation: use translateY transforms where possible and limit reflows; run perf spike.
Risk: Gesture heuristics misfire on trackpads. Mitigation: tune velocity threshold and expose pref in user settings for power users.
Risk: Increased header clutter. Mitigation: use transient coachmarks and hide hints after first use; put advanced toggle in settings.
